newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end trade in negative territory.
newsitem.headline: German shares end trade in negative territory.

text.p: German shares ended trade on Thursday lower, having fallen sharply in high-volume late afternoon trade on profit-taking, weakness on Wall Street and a softer dollar against the mark.

The IBIS DAX index ended down 19.78 points at 4,203.91, having earlier fallen as low as 4,182.40 points after Wall Street wobbled in early trade and there was finally some evidence of profit-taking in the market.
The DAX index ended bourse trade earlier on at 4,227.31 points, up 26.07 points or 0.62 percent.
"There's a bit of profit-taking going on, a lot of nervousness and people are watching Wall Street pretty closely," a Frankfurt trader said.
The Dow Jones Industrial index opened at a stable level of 8,037.02 points, but lost ground soon after to fall to 8,005.44 points. But the 8,000-point threshold appeared to be holding.
The dollar weakened against the mark to 1.7895 in afternoon trade, which hit German exporters, especially carmakers and chemicals.

BASF AG and Hoechst AG ended down 11 pfennigs at 71.24 marks and 1.73 marks at 83.90 respectively, although the other firm in the big three chemical companies, Bayer AG, bucked the trend to close 17 pfennigs higher at 75.90 marks.
Volkswagen AG, which has been a stock market darling for many months, was lower amid market speculation that the stock had been downgraded by an investment house.
VW shares took a further hit on news that the carmaker has recalled 12,000 Sharan minivans and the share ended down 25.50 marks at 1,440 marks.
Other car stocks were also hit. Daimler-Benz AG ended down 1.60 marks at 151.70 marks, Porsche preference shares down 82 marks at 2,700 marks, while BMW AG was down 14 marks at 1,516 marks.
Other shares in the news included retailer Karstadt, which had been rising all week on speculation that Germany's WCM group would be taking a stake in the group.
WCM denied an interest, but Karstadt shares were still buoyant as electronic trade ended, up 4.50 marks at 693 marks.
